summary:
Second, trustworthy measurement of onboarding-KB value. After fixing the circular v1 harness (keyword-graded → fake 0%→100%), the honest harness (applied-correctness LLM judge + 4 control probes + guard requiring cold-rate strictly in (0,1)) ran on the orchestrator repo: cold 11/11, kb 11/11, kb_earned_project=0 → guard trustworthy:false, DEGENERATE. The cold agent answered all 7 project-specific probes correctly WITHOUT the KB, by reading the source. Combined with the v5 NO-WIN, the structural finding is robust: for project knowledge a capable model can recover from the code, an ingested KB adds nothing to CORRECTNESS. Onboarding-KB value, if real, lives in non-recoverable knowledge (decision rationale, reverted approaches, unwritten conventions, cross-session/cross-repo memory) or in COST/exploration-reduction — not correctness on recoverable facts. Decision needed: re-target probes at non-recoverable knowledge, switch the loop's metric to cost/speed-to-correct, or accept correctness isn't the case and justify ingest on other grounds. Build of /11 learning loop is HELD until the loop optimizes a signal that actually moves.</summary>
</invoke>
